[32130 Fundamentals of Data Analytics | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject equips you with both theoretical and hands-on experience of data analytics, the process of extracting meaningful insights from large data sets. You'll learn statistical methods and data visualisation techniques to explore and process vast volumes of data, and unsupervised as well as supervised techniques to discover patterns and insights for knowledge discovery. The subject synthesises cutting-edge research and practice, preparing you to lead data analytics projects that transform data into commercially valuable information.

[32130 Fundamentals of Data Analytics | Learning and teaching activities]
Subject presentation includes combined lecture and workshop sessions and practical data analytics tasks for the assignments. Students will need to undertake preparation using material on Canvas to make effective use of their workshop time. Lectures will present the theoretical aspects of data analytics, including guest lectures about case studies of real-world business applications of data mining techniques. The workshop sessions focus on hands-on experience in data analytics and data analytics tools, and understanding and interpretation of the results. Practical assignments can be performed anywhere.

Prepreparation will help students to participate in the in-class individual and group exercises. Regular zero mark quizzes throughout the semester will allow students to gauge their progress

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32130 Fundamentals of Data Analytics | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Scope framed data informed business problems using contextual, ethical, and stakeholder awareness. (B.1)
SLO2: Design data analytics approaches to business objectives and data constraints. (C.1)
SLO3: Use appropriate data analytics methods to describe and implement descriptive and predictive analytics solutions. (D.1)
SLO4: Communicate data analytics methods and insights effectively in oral and written forms, demonstrating responsible and critical collaboration with AI tools. (E.1)
